findings.title: Cache is set before the limit check, so a retry bypasses the device limit entirely
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes the device key into the local cache (29-minute TTL) before calling anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the configured device limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for a new device and Anonymous.Authenticate (client.go) rejects the request — but the cache entry has already been written and is never removed. Any subsequent request from the same device within 29 minutes hits the cache in tagDeviceUI, returns nil, and Authenticate succeeds, even though the device was never persisted and is never counted toward the limit. A brand-new device therefore only has to send its request twice to get anonymous access past the limit, and this is repeatable after each cache expiry (first request fails, then ~29 minutes of access). The cache key should be set only after a successful store call, or explicitly deleted when CreateOrUpdateDevice returns an error.

findings.title: Device limit check-then-insert is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit by running CountDevices and then, only if count < deviceLimit, executing the INSERT. These are two separate statements with no transaction or locking. Concurrent anonymous requests carrying distinct new device IDs — or requests landing on different Grafana replicas in an HA setup — can all observe a count below the limit and then all insert, so the stored device count can exceed deviceLimit by an arbitrary margin under a burst of new devices (e.g., bot/scraper traffic). If the limit is meant to be a hard cap, the count-and-insert must be done atomically (single transaction with locking), or the overshoot should be explicitly accepted and documented.

findings.title: No test for the allowed path: existing device must still be updated when the limit is reached
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only asserts that a new device is rejected once the limit is reached. The complementary and more important branch — a device that already exists in anon_device must still be updated via updateDevice and allowed in while count >= deviceLimit — has no test, and neither does the propagation through Anonymous.Authenticate in client.go, which now fails authentication on ErrDeviceLimitReached. A regression in updateDevice's WHERE clause (for example a wrong updated_at window) would lock out every existing anonymous device as soon as the limit is hit, and nothing in this PR's tests would catch that.

findings.title: New device_limit option is not documented in defaults.ini/sample.ini or the admin docs
findings.body: readAuthSettings adds support for device_limit under [auth.anonymous], but the option is not added to conf/defaults.ini or conf/sample.ini, where every other auth.anonymous key is listed with an explanatory comment, and the configure-grafana documentation is not updated either. Operators have no discoverable way to learn the setting exists or that the default of 0 means the limit is disabled. The PR's own checklist requires docs to be updated for new configuration.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined infers the property type as undefined
findings.body: In GrafanaBootConfig, the new field is declared as `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` with no type annotation, so TypeScript infers the class property's type as `undefined` (the `implements GrafanaConfig` clause does not widen inferred member types). Any frontend code reading config.anonymousDeviceLimit will see the type `undefined` and cannot compare or otherwise use it as a number without a cast, which defeats the purpose of exposing the value to the frontend. It should be declared as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`.
